> **Experimental.** From a list of CVR numbers to analysable accounting
> data, in one package: search Erhvervsstyrelsens distribution service,
> download what it found, and parse the machine-readable filings. Danish
> and Greenlandic companies alike — Greenland’s own register was folded
> into CVR in 2018, and its companies file under the same taxonomy.
> Split out of [daos](https://github.com/dataniel/daos), and named for
> the functions it has always been made of.

## Installation

``` r
pak::pak("dataniel/cvrr")
```

## The whole route

``` r
library(cvrr)

cvr_query(
  cvr          = c("12345678", "87654321"),
  enddate_from = "2020-01-01",
  enddate_to   = "2024-12-31"
) |>
  cvr_search(contact = "you@example.com") |>
  cvr_hits() |>
  cvr_download("materiale/xbrl")

# a whole directory, taxonomy and all
x <- read_xbrl("materiale/xbrl")

a <- xbrl_accounts(x)
a$company           # who the company is
a$location          # where it is
a$audit             # who audited it, who filed it, with what tool
a$checks            # whether any of it adds up
a$income_statement  # lines, in statement order
a$balance           # lines, with the ones the filer left out derived
a$movements         # the fixed asset note, movement by movement
a$prose             # what management wrote
```

Four functions to find and fetch, one to read, one to divide up. Nothing
in between is manual: no numeric conversion, no period argument, no
binding the filings together by hand.

Every table opens with the same key — `cvr`, `name`, `period_start`,
`period_end` — and ends with `file`, so moving between them needs no
looking and every figure can be traced back to the document it came
from. The two statements carry `reconciled` on every row, so filtering
to the lines that add up needs no join, and `checks` gathers the
per-filing verdicts in one place.

## Two forms, one of them useful

A filing usually exists as both a PDF and an XML file. The XML is XBRL —
the machine-readable form — and
[`read_xbrl()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/read_xbrl.md)
turns it into a tibble with one row per reported fact: its value, its
context dates, its unit, the namespace that identifies it in the
taxonomy, and every dimension the context carries,
`ConsolidatedSoloDimension` included.

The PDF is the human-readable version, and there is no parser for it
here. For older filings, small companies, and reports that are a scan of
paper, the PDF is the only digital trace, and turning one back into a
table is a different kind of work. That is what
[taxmill](https://github.com/dataniel/taxmill) is for.

## Signs

XBRL amounts often arrive without a meaningful sign: costs can be
reported as positive numbers, and the convention varies between
preparers.
[`find_signs()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/find_signs.md)
recovers them, because an income statement has to reconcile — it
searches for the `+1`/`-1`/`0` assignment that makes the line items sum
to the reported total.

``` r
find_signs(income, elementid, value,
           total_label = "ProfitLoss",
           by = c(cvr, period_end))
```

Nothing is dropped: every row comes back with a `status` of `unique`,
`ambiguous`, `unsolved`, `no_total` or `duplicate_total`, and items that
every candidate assignment agreed on are filled in even when the group
as a whole is ambiguous.

The taxonomy publishes these weights too, in its calculation linkbase.
The two routes are independent, so running both is a genuine cross-check
rather than a restatement — see
[`vignette("cvrr")`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/articles/cvrr.md).

## The taxonomy is where the meaning lives

An XBRL instance carries facts and no readable text at all: labels, the
statement hierarchy and the debit/credit markings are in the taxonomy
the filing names in one `schemaRef`. Point
[`read_taxonomy()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/read_taxonomy.md)
at the package Erhvervsstyrelsen publishes and the rest follows.

``` r
tax  <- read_taxonomy("XBRL20241001.zip")
tidy <- read_xbrl("data/xml/13645183_2024-12-31.xml") |>
  add_taxonomy(tax)

check_statement(tidy)
```

Every figure arrives with a stable accounting code from the taxonomy’s
own numbering, its Danish label, whether it is debit or credit, and —
decided by the taxonomy’s declared dimension default rather than by
guesswork — whether it is the group’s figure or the parent company’s.

## Using the service well

[`cvr_search()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/cvr_search.md)
requires a `contact` email address and sends it as the `User-Agent`
header: Erhvervsstyrelsen asks requests to identify their sender. The
function refuses an empty contact, but it cannot check that the address
is honest — that part is yours.
[`vignette("cvrr")`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/articles/cvrr.md)
covers the rest of the habits worth having: query volume, `scroll` for
complete results, testing small first, and the legal frame around
*reklamebeskyttelse*.

## Functions

In the order the route runs.

**Find and fetch**

| Function                                                                      | Description                                               |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| [`cvr_query()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/cvr_query.md)       | Build an Elasticsearch query for published annual reports |
| [`cvr_search()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/cvr_search.md)     | Send a query to Erhvervsstyrelsens distribution service   |
| [`cvr_hits()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/cvr_hits.md)         | Flatten a response into a tibble, one row per document    |
| [`cvr_download()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/cvr_download.md) | Download the documents found by a search                  |

**Read, and divide up**

| Function                                                                          | Description                                                                                                                                                |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`read_xbrl()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/read_xbrl.md)           | Read one filing, a list of them, or a directory, into one tibble with the taxonomy on it                                                                   |
| [`xbrl_accounts()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/xbrl_accounts.md)   | The filings divided into eight keyed tables: the company, where it is, the audit trail, the checks, the two statements, the fixed asset note and the prose |
| [`xbrl_company()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/xbrl_company.md)     | The company behind a filing: identity, legal form, class, auditor, employees, activity                                                                     |
| [`xbrl_lines()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/xbrl_lines.md)         | One statement, line by line, in statement order                                                                                                            |
| [`xbrl_movements()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/xbrl_movements.md) | The fixed asset note as a roll-forward: cost, depreciation and revaluation at each end of the year, and the movements between                              |

**Name and place the facts**

| Function                                                                              | Description                                                            |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`add_taxonomy()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/add_taxonomy.md)         | Give a filing’s facts their statement, code, label and sign convention |
| [`read_taxonomy()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/read_taxonomy.md)       | Open a taxonomy package and read its catalog, labels and defaults      |
| `cvrr_line`, `cvrr_entry`                                                             | Twelve taxonomies as tables, so no package is needed on disk           |
| [`xbrl_fill()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/xbrl_fill.md)               | Derive the subtotals and components a filing left out                  |
| [`xbrl_resolve()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/xbrl_resolve.md)         | Choose between two figures reported for the same line                  |
| [`xbrl_period()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/xbrl_period.md)           | Read the accounting period a filing declares for itself                |
| [`xbrl_note_tables()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/xbrl_note_tables.md) | Read the tables inside a filing’s text notes                           |

**Does it add up?**

| Function                                                                              | Description                                                           |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`check_statement()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/check_statement.md)   | Reconcile every subtotal against the lines below it                   |
| [`check_cascade()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/check_cascade.md)       | Reconcile an income statement step by step to the result for the year |
| [`check_breakdown()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/check_breakdown.md)   | Reconcile a dimensional breakdown against the line it breaks down     |
| [`check_movement()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/check_movement.md)     | Reconcile an opening balance and its movements to the closing balance |
| [`check_continuity()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/check_continuity.md) | Does the balance a company closed on reopen in the next filing?       |
| [`check_inclusion()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/check_inclusion.md)   | Find lines a note says are contained in another                       |
| [`find_signs()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/find_signs.md)             | Recover the signs that reconcile line items to a total                |

## Where the package stops

cvrr hands out the accounting figures the filings actually carry, with
the label, the code and the sign convention the taxonomy gives them.
Mapping those onto a particular statistic’s variable definitions is
yours to make: which element counts as turnover depends on the
definitions in force, and a package that decided it for you would be
wrong the year they changed.

  : Build an Elasticsearch query for CVR annual reports

  : Send a query to the CVR distribution service

  : Read XBRL filings
- [`xbrl_accounts()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/xbrl_accounts.md)
  : A pile of filings as the tables an analysis reads

- [`xbrl_company()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/xbrl_company.md)

  [`cvrr_line`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/cvrr_taxonomy_tables.md)

  : The Danish annual report taxonomies, as tables

  : Choose between two figures reported for the same line

- [`xbrl_note_tables()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/xbrl_note_tables.md)
  : Read the tables inside a filing's text notes

## Does it add up?

- [`check_statement()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/check_statement.md)
  : Reconcile a statement against its own hierarchy
- [`check_cascade()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/check_cascade.md)
  : Reconcile an income statement step by step
- [`check_breakdown()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/check_breakdown.md)
  : Reconcile a dimensional breakdown against the line it breaks down

  : Reconcile an opening balance and its movements to the closing

  : Find lines a note says are contained in another line
- [`find_signs()`](https://dataniel.github.io/cvrr/reference/find_signs.md)
